founding: The old songs say this is the very ford where Aldren the Ford-King crossed in {caldor} BL to found the High Kingdom of Caldor. The council dates the charter {year} AL.
visit: The {party} hear the old story of {region}. {history}

ages.name: The Age of Making
ages.text: Haldor struck the first mountains on his anvil, Sylvaine grew the first forests in the silence after, and the Stormmother poured the seas. Ysolde opened her book and began to write down every true thing. The first peoples woke where their makers had worked: giants on the high places, elves under the trees, dwarves inside the stone.

ages.name: The Elder Age
ages.text: Giants, elves and dwarves built the first realms, and the first great dragon burned them.

ages.name: The Age of Sands and Serpents
ages.text: Masked god-kings ruled the green river land that is now desert, and serpent-priests ruled the fens, until the Stormmother took the rain from one and drowned the other.

ages.name: The Age of Crowns
ages.text: The High Kingdom of Caldor rose at a river ford, ruled from the coast to the sands, and died in the first Long Night when its last king would not cross the Ferryman's river.

ages.name: The Age of Splinters
ages.text: Caldor's lords fought over its crown for seven centuries, the harbours made themselves free cities, and the orc hosts of the Red Tide burned the Marches.

ages.name: The Age of Lanterns
ages.text: The Crown League swore to answer one another's beacons, and the frontier began to fill in again, town by town: points of light.

powers.name: The Stonekings
powers.text: Giant kings who ruled the high places from halls cut into whole mountains. Vermithrax burned them out, and their broken steadings are still the largest ruins in the world.
powers.heirs: Hill and frost giant clans; the giants in tribe menaces.

powers.name: The Rime Clans
powers.text: The Stonekings' last frost giant clans, who held the ice until human jarls drove them into the glaciers.
powers.heirs: Frost giants and frostwights in the Rimefell.

powers.name: The Frost-Sworn Halls
powers.text: Free jarls in whale-bone halls under the aurora. Caldor sent three armies north, and the jarls sent them home in boxes. They have never knelt to anyone.
powers.heirs: The frost-sworn, who respect strength and despise tribute.

powers.name: The Wyrm-Tyranny
powers.text: Vermithrax, the first great dragon, burned the Stonekings' halls and ruled giant and dwarf alike for seven centuries, until dwarves and elves together bound him in sleep under a mountain.
powers.heirs: The dragon broods in the beast menaces; Vermithrax himself, asleep.

powers.name: The Smith-King's Holds
powers.text: Surface holds raised by the dwarves who forged Vermithrax's chains. They guarded the high passes for three thousand years, until the Red Tide came over them.
powers.heirs: The dwarf holds of today.

powers.name: The Red Tide
powers.text: Ghorvak's orc hosts came down from the mountains and burned the Crown Marches. Sellswords sworn to Brannoch broke them; the Wolfsbane Company kept its name from that war.
powers.heirs: The orc and goblin warbands in the tribe menaces.

powers.name: Warrens and Free Holds
powers.text: Orc warrens and dwarf holds share the passes in a long, bloody truce that neither side has ever called peace.
powers.heirs: The dwarves and the warbands the town meets today.

powers.name: The Chained Mountain
powers.text: The mountain where Vermithrax sleeps in the Smith-King's chains has smoked for four thousand years. The Smith-King died at his furnace forging them.
powers.heirs: If no other power rises to threaten the land, the Old Wyrm wakes.

powers.name: Khaz Varrund, the Deep Realm
powers.text: The dwarves dug a kingdom under the mountains, deeper every century. It fell when its miners broke into something below that breathed. The Vault That Breathes and the Glimmering Rot are its last halls.
powers.heirs: The dwarf holds and the deep gnomes.

powers.name: The Gnome Workings
powers.text: Deep gnomes stayed in the Deep Realm's lower workings when the dwarves fled, and have mapped every tunnel since.
powers.heirs: The deep gnomes, who trade clockwork and maps of the deep ways.

powers.name: The Court of First Leaves
powers.text: The elves' court once held every forest in the world. It never fell. It only shrank, a little each age, into the twilight glades where the seasons run out of order, and its hags and lords keep bargains the Court broke long ago.
powers.heirs: The elf enclaves; the hags and fey in the schemer menaces.

powers.name: The River Tribes
powers.text: The first human tribes farmed the river valleys, fought each other, and paid the Coil's tithe in eels.
powers.heirs: The villagers.

powers.name: The High Kingdom of Caldor
powers.text: Aldren the Ford-King united the river tribes at a ford on a cold northern river. At its height Caldor ruled from the Salt Reach to the edge of the sands, built the roads and castles whose ruins fill the Crownlands, and made Ostrava of the Even Scale its god. Its last king, Maudren, bought a way past the Ferryman's river, and the dead of every battlefield in Caldor walked: the first Long Night.
powers.heirs: The barrow-kings, the usurpers, the templars, and every village in the heartland.

powers.name: The Crown Marches
powers.text: Caldor's surviving lords each claimed the crown and fought over it for seven centuries. Halflings quietly settled the farmland they emptied.
powers.heirs: The robber barons in the rival menaces; the halflings.

powers.name: The Crown League
powers.text: Free cities and tired marcher lords swore to answer one another's beacons. Under the League's peace the Compass Lodge began paying adventurers to clear the old roads, and new towns were founded on the frontier.
powers.heirs: Your town.

powers.name: The Free Ports
powers.text: Caldor's harbours shut their gates on the Long Night and opened them as free cities. The Gilded Scale and the Quiet Hand were born on their wharves.
powers.heirs: The port folk.

powers.name: The Coil
powers.text: A serpent-priest theocracy of the fens, served by lizardfolk. When the sea rose its temples sank with their saints still in them.
powers.heirs: The lizardfolk, who will not go to the Drowned Temple.

powers.name: The Sunken Fens
powers.text: The lizardfolk outlived their masters and keep the fens in stilt villages above the drowned temples.
powers.heirs: The lizardfolk.

powers.name: The Ninefold Throne of Ashkaar
powers.text: Nine masked god-kings ruled a green river land in turn. The ninth tried to bind the Stormmother to bring the floods on command, and she took the rain away for good. The empire dried into dunes; its ninth queen became a lich rather than die with it.
powers.heirs: The oasis caravaneers; the Silent Knife; Ashkara the Deathless.

powers.name: The Dry Centuries
powers.text: For eighteen centuries the sands belonged to the tombs and whatever walked out of them.
powers.heirs: The buried cities of the Duneglass.

powers.name: The Oasis Cities
powers.text: Ashkaar's grandchildren reopened the old caravan roads, and Aurel's worship travelled with them.
powers.heirs: The caravaneers, who know which tombs to leave shut.

events.text: Khaz Varrund breaks into the deep
The Lamp ends the first Long Night

tempersDoc: Each campaign rolls one temper per menace kind (a pure function of the seed): the same kind of foe can be warlike in one game and sensible in the next. ambitions multiply the lineage's weights, strike multiplies the days between strikes, will adds to Discipline.

tempers.name: warlike
tempers.text: In this age the warbands are warlike: they raid for glory and answer every slight with fire.

tempers.name: sensible
tempers.text: In this age the clans are sensible: they hold their valleys hard but leave alone what leaves them alone.

tempers.name: feuding
tempers.text: In this age the clans are feuding among themselves, and a strong chief can be bargained with or played against a rival.

tempers.name: restless
tempers.text: In this age the dead are restless: the old graves stir with every new moon and every new grief.

tempers.name: dormant
tempers.text: In this age the dead mostly sleep, and wake only for those who dig where they lie.

tempers.name: marching
tempers.text: In this age the dead march in ranks, as if someone long gone were still giving the orders.

tempers.name: patient
tempers.text: In this age the old courts in the dark are patient: they buy, they marry and they wait.

tempers.name: cruel
tempers.text: In this age the old courts are cruel and bored, and hunt for sport between their schemes.

tempers.name: courtly
tempers.text: In this age the old courts are courtly: they would rather have the town bow than bleed.

tempers.name: proud
tempers.text: In this age the great wyrms are proud: they want to be feared and named, and flattery is their weakness.

tempers.name: wrathful
tempers.text: In this age the great wyrms are wrathful, and burn first and count the hoard after.

tempers.name: slumbering
tempers.text: In this age the great wyrms mostly sleep on their gold, and woe to whoever wakes one.

tempers.name: ravenous
tempers.text: In this age the beasts of the wild are ravenous, pushed down from the heights by something worse.

tempers.name: territorial
tempers.text: In this age the beasts keep to their own ground, and only those who trespass need fear them.

tempers.name: cutthroat
tempers.text: In this age the free companies are cutthroat, and a rival will knife a bounty out from under you.

tempers.name: honourable
tempers.text: In this age the free companies keep to a code, and even a rival will not strike a town unprovoked.

tempers.name: zealous
tempers.text: In this age the cults are zealous, and preach in the open where they once whispered.

tempers.name: secretive
tempers.text: In this age the cults keep to cellars and code-words, and their hand is seen only after it has closed.

tempers.name: bargaining
tempers.text: In this age the fiends bargain before they burn, and the worst of them are polite.

tempers.name: ravening
tempers.text: In this age the fiends come through hungry, and nothing on the near side of a doorway is safe.

lineages.title: heirs of the Red Tide
lineages.motive: {leader} carries Ghorvak's war-drum and means to finish what the Red Tide began in 380 AL: every lowland hall burned and every road the orcs' own.

lineages.title: the Warren clans
lineages.motive: The Warren clans breed faster than the passes can feed them, and {leader} wants the valleys below for the spill.

lineages.title: the Stonekings' last kin
lineages.motive: {leader} still calls the high places the Stonekings' halls, and counts every wall built in them as theft.

lineages.title: the last of the Rime Clans
lineages.motive: {leader} keeps the Rime Clans' old claim: everything the ice once covered is theirs, and the ice is coming back.

lineages.title: the Hollow King's court
lineages.motive: {leader} swore to Caldor and was never let go. The dead of {seat} still march for a crown that fell twelve centuries ago, and want it back on the ford where {town} stands.

lineages.title: the dead of the Ninefold Throne
lineages.motive: {leader} keeps Ashkaar's oldest law: every living thing kneels, and serves again after death.

lineages.title: the drowned of the Coil
lineages.motive: The sea took the Coil's temples with their saints still in them. {leader} wants the living down in the water too.

lineages.title: brokers of the Last Door
lineages.motive: {leader} deals in the kind of bargain that ended Caldor: a wish granted now, a door opened later.

lineages.title: oathbreakers of the Court of First Leaves
lineages.motive: {leader} keeps a bargain the Court of First Leaves broke long ago, and collects on it from anyone who lives on old forest ground.

lineages.title: the Coil's whisperers
lineages.motive: The serpent-priests of the Coil never died, only went under. {leader} buys towns one councillor at a time, as the Coil bought the river tribes.

lineages.title: the Wyrm-Tyranny's broods
lineages.motive: The Wyrm-Tyranny bred monsters as hounds and loosed them when it fell. {leader} is of their line.

lineages.title: Vermithrax's brood
lineages.motive: {leader} has the Old Wyrm's blood and the Old Wyrm's memory: the peaks were theirs once, and every hoard in them.

lineages.title: the Ash Regents
lineages.motive: When the Wyrm-Tyranny fell, its younger wyrms scattered and named themselves regents of a throne that no longer stood. {leader} means to sit on it, and every valley that pays tribute is one more step toward the old crown.

lineages.title: beasts of the Elder wood
lineages.motive: {leader} is older than the fields. The Elder Age's forest remembers it, and it wants the clearings back.

lineages.title: a marcher house
lineages.motive: {leader} claims descent from Caldor's marcher lords, and means to be the first king on the ford in twelve hundred years.

lineages.title: Free Port corsairs
lineages.motive: {leader} sails under the old Free Port charters, which say any road a ship can reach is a road it may tax.

lineages.title: a caravan prince of the Oasis Cities
lineages.motive: {leader} owns wells, and in the sands that is the same as owning people. {town}'s market would make a fine well.

lineages.title: the Hollow King's choir
lineages.motive: {leader} sings the hymn of King Maudren's court singers: the grave is a door, and the Hollow King waits behind it to be let back in.

lineages.title: creditors of the Last Door
lineages.motive: Caldor opened the Last Door and never paid for it. {leader} has come through to collect, and {town} stands on Caldor's ford.

lineages.title: Caldor's river tribes
lineages.motive: They want a strong town between their fields and the hills, as Caldor once was.

lineages.title: the halflings of the Marches
lineages.motive: They want the roads open and the larders full, and they remember who fed them in the Red Tide.

lineages.title: heirs of Khaz Varrund
lineages.motive: They want the deep halls back, and every dragon's hoard counted.

lineages.title: the Court of First Leaves
lineages.motive: They want the old forest left standing, and Caldor's axes remembered.

lineages.title: the gnomes of the lower workings
lineages.motive: They want every tunnel mapped and every map sold.

lineages.title: the Coil's last servants
lineages.motive: They want the drowned temples left alone.

lineages.title: keepers of the Dawn Gate
lineages.motive: They want the dead kept down, as their order has since the first Long Night.

lineages.title: the Free Ports
lineages.motive: They want trade, and no crown over it.

lineages.title: the Frost-Sworn Halls
lineages.motive: They want strength honoured and tribute refused.

lineages.title: the tomb-cats of Ashkaar
lineages.motive: They want the old kings' debts paid at last, and every secret in the sands to be theirs to sell.

lineages.title: the nesters in the giants' halls
lineages.motive: They want the high places left to the sky, and the giants never to come home.

lineages.title: the awakened temple guard of Caldor
lineages.motive: They want the oath they were woken for kept: the shrines guarded until a rightful king returns.

lineages.title: Ashkaar's grandchildren
lineages.motive: They want the caravan roads open and the old tombs shut.

lineages.title: Free Port moneylenders
lineages.motive: It wants every debt on the frontier written in its book.

lineages.title: the League's road-openers
lineages.motive: It wants Caldor's old roads cleared and paid for, one bounty at a time.

lineages.title: the Crown League of 724 AL
lineages.motive: It wants every town on the frontier answering the beacons.

lineages.title: the knights of the Dawn Gate
lineages.motive: It wants the dead kept down, as it did through the first Long Night.

lineages.title: the Free Port guilds
lineages.motive: It wants fair weight, fair price, and the council's ear, as it has had in the Free Ports since 212 AL.

lineages.title: King Maudren's court singers
lineages.motive: It wants the grave opened and the Hollow King let back in.

lineages.title: the Lantern Mother's hidden servants
lineages.motive: It wants no tyrant to rise on the ford again, and works in the dark against any that tries.

lineages.title: the wharf-thieves of the Free Ports
lineages.motive: It wants a cut of everything, and quiet streets to take it from.

lineages.title: the mask-killers of Ashkaar
lineages.motive: It keeps the Ninefold Throne's trade in quiet deaths, and wants only its price.

lineages.title: keepers of Sylvaine's pact
lineages.motive: It wants the old pact between field and forest kept, and the axes counted.

lineages.title: scholars of fallen Caldor
lineages.motive: It wants everything Caldor forgot, and everything it should have.

lineages.title: veterans of the Red Tide war
lineages.motive: It wants paying, as it was when it broke Ghorvak's hosts.

lineages.title: Vermithrax's last brood
lineages.motive: It wants the hoard the Wyrm-Tyranny lost, and every lesser dragon out of the sky its father ruled.

lineages.title: the drowned Coil's oracles
lineages.motive: It wants bargains struck and favours owed, as the Coil's oracles took the river tribes' tithe in eels and names.

lineages.title: Caldor's surviving court wizards
lineages.motive: It wants a throne to stand behind again, an enclave in every rich town and first claim on every relic in the wilds.

lineages.title: League levies who stayed under arms
lineages.motive: It wants a war worth the pay, and a town that remembers the League kept the beacons lit.

lineages.title: Free Port marines for hire up the rivers
lineages.motive: It wants silver, plunder, and no crown telling it where it may sail.

lineages.title: the Smith-King's oath-bound shieldwalls
lineages.motive: It wants every contract kept to the letter, and the old holds' honour restored one paid war at a time.

lineages.title: lancers of the oasis cities
lineages.motive: It wants gold enough to buy back the wells its families lost to the caravan princes.

lineages.title: the marcher lords' griffon riders
lineages.motive: It wants the roads watched from the sky as the marches once were, and riders who answer to the town rather than to any lord.

lineages.title: the hold-wrights' lodges, carried down from the high passes
lineages.motive: It wants walls and halls raised by its own hands and to its own measure, and no town that builds without first asking the lodge.

lineages.title: smiths who still swear by the Smith-King's anvil
lineages.motive: It wants every blade and hinge in town struck at its forges, and a watch armed well enough to keep the forges safe.

lineages.title: the halfling brew-houses that kept the marches drinking through seven centuries of war
lineages.motive: It wants feast days, light taxes and full taps, and a town that remembers who kept it cheerful.

lineages.title: the river tribes' field-moots
lineages.motive: It wants new fields broken every spring and no lord, mayor or tithe-man taking more of the harvest than the old custom allows.

lineages.title: the free ports' cloth-halls and chandlers' rows
lineages.motive: It wants a market where honest goods sell at honest prices, and a town hall that taxes trade as lightly as the free ports did.

lineages.title: gnome riggers out of the Gnome Workings
lineages.motive: It wants the sky opened the way the Workings opened the deep: every road a straight line, and the town that learns to fly ahead of every rival.

lineages.title: beast-wardens sworn under the Court of First Leaves
lineages.motive: It wants the wild's creatures understood rather than slaughtered, and a town that learns to live beside them.

lineages.title: the Coil's old relic-brokers, gone respectable
lineages.motive: It wants every cursed thing the ruins give up to pass through its hands, and a price on each of them.

lineages.title: the moon-markets of the Hollow Hill
lineages.motive: It wants bargains struck and kept, and a town that remembers the fey were trading here before it had a name.

lineages.title: the star-readers of the oasis cities
lineages.motive: It wants the heavens read truly and the town warned in time, and its oracle believed when it matters.

lineages.title: the deep-wardens of fallen Khaz Varrund
lineages.motive: It wants what Khaz Varrund woke kept below, and never again a town that digs without a gate and a warden at the bottom of the stair.

lineages.title: a chapter of Caldor's last knightly orders
lineages.motive: It wants the oaths Caldor broke kept by someone, and the town to be worth guarding.

lineages.title: the free ports' distilling guilds
lineages.motive: It wants a town that asks few questions about smoke and pays well for what comes out of it.

lineages.title: an outpost of the Gnome Workings
lineages.motive: It wants to build something no one has built before, and a town rich enough to pay for the attempt.

lineages.title: the fighting-games of the Ninefold Throne
lineages.motive: It wants crowds, champions and a name that echoes in the stands of every city.

lineages.title: the marcher lords' remembrancers
lineages.motive: It wants every deed of the town sung true, or at least sung well, so that the town is never forgotten.

lineages.title: the beacon-temples of the League
lineages.motive: It wants every god who kept the League's lamps lit given ground and honour in the town, and the town to remember who sheltered it.

lineages.title: the League's muster-halls, turned to bounty work
lineages.motive: It wants every company on the frontier registered, paid fairly and brought home.

lineages.title: a caravanserai on the oasis cities' pattern
lineages.motive: It wants the far roads open and the town on every caravan master's map.

lineages.title: a seedling of the Court of First Leaves
lineages.motive: It wants Sylvaine's old pact kept inside the walls as well as outside them: a living place the town does not pave.

lineages.title: a marcher road-house
lineages.motive: It wants a full house, a good story and every rumour on the road told first at its bar.

lineages.title: the last shelves of Caldor's royal libraries
lineages.motive: It wants every book scattered by the Long Night found and brought home, and read by someone wise enough not to repeat Maudren's bargain.

lineages.title: a Stoneking's buried hall
lineages.motive: It wants the giant kings' halls opened, mapped and emptied by the living before whatever stayed down there finds its own way up.

lineages.title: the League's old custom of envoys
lineages.motive: It wants every people that answers a beacon to have a door in the town, and every quarrel settled at a table instead of on a road.

lineages.title: a ring raised on the pattern of the Ashkaari gates
lineages.motive: It wants the ways the Ninefold Throne opened kept open, and kept better than Ashkaar kept them.

lineages.title: the halls where Caldor's kings hung their champions' shields
lineages.motive: It wants every hero who served the town remembered, and the founding banner home on its pedestal.

lineages.title: a dragon of the Old Wyrm's brood that chose a treaty over a throne
lineages.motive: It wants to be admired, fed and consulted, and to prove that a dragon can keep a town without burning it.

lineages.title: acolyte
lineages.motive: served at a League temple, lighting the beacon-lamps

lineages.title: criminal
lineages.motive: learned the trade on the wharves of the Free Ports

lineages.title: sage
lineages.motive: copied Caldor's old records for the Unshut Book

lineages.title: soldier
lineages.motive: stood in a League levy when the beacons were lit

lineages.title: caravan guard
lineages.motive: rode guard on the Oasis road, where water costs more than wine

lineages.title: disgraced councillor
lineages.motive: sat on a League town's council until a scandal

lineages.title: fog runner
lineages.motive: ran messages between the old march forts

lineages.title: frontier settler
lineages.motive: came with the first League wagons to clear the frontier

lineages.title: guild apprentice
lineages.motive: apprenticed to a Gilded Scale master

lineages.title: herb gatherer
lineages.motive: gathered herbs in the Court of First Leaves' borderwoods

lineages.title: lapsed initiate
lineages.motive: knelt in a Hollow Choir cellar until they saw what it was for

lineages.title: plague survivor
lineages.motive: walked out of a village a tomb-plague out of the sands burned

lineages.title: relic peddler
lineages.motive: sold Caldor's relics, some of them real

lineages.title: toll collector
lineages.motive: sat at a marcher lord's bridge gate

lineages.title: turncoat raider
lineages.motive: rode with a Warren warband until they could not stomach it

lineages.title: wall mason
lineages.motive: laid stone the way the Smith-King's masons taught
